 The Mandalorian premiered in 2019, serving as a flagship project for the launch of Disney+. What's important to bear in mind here is that this was seven years after George Lucas sold the Star Wars franchise to Disney. As such, despite being the beloved space opera's creator, Lucas no longer had any direct input into its creative direction. That is still the case today.

 That being said, Lucas has understandably weighed in from time to time on Star Wars projects that have been made since he cashed in. One such project is The Mandalorian , which current Lucasfilm President Dave Filoni has been heavily involved with as a producer, writer, and director. Filoni worked closely with Lucas on Star Wars: The Clone Wars , most of which was made before the Disney deal.
 As a result, it won't be surprising to learn that the two men have remained in touch and are still close friends, even though Filoni is now the steward of the franchise instead. Via this continuing dynamic, Lucas has commented on certain elements of Disney-era Star Wars shows , including The Mandalorian . Years later, one of his biggest concerns about the series still hasn't been properly addressed.
 Grogu Still Hasn't Had the "Proper Amount of Training" That Lucas Wanted
 Disney 
 The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season 2 was published in 2022 and provided some fun and interesting additional context for the Disney+ series' second batch of episodes. In the book, Filoni stated that Lucas' “main concern was that [Grogu] has to have a proper amount of training.” Given that Season 2 ends with Grogu leaving with Luke to be trained as a Jedi, Lucas' concern makes sense.
 However, since then, Star Wars has only made a token effort to address Lucas' point. Although The Book of Boba Fett showed Luke briefly training Grogu in the ways of the Force, it hardly felt like a "proper amount" of training. Regardless, Grogu continues to use the Force to aid in his adventures with Din Djarin (Pedro Pascal). 
 This is also in conflict with Ahsoka's (Rosario Dawson) claims that Grogu's powers would (and should be allowed to) fade with time if not given the proper training. So far, that doesn't seem to be the case. The idea that Grogu would grow up to become both a Jedi and a Mandalorian has long been teased as a compelling possibility, but the franchise seems unwilling to commit to either fate for him. 
 The "Proper Amount of Training" Has Always Been Pretty Nebulous in Star Wars

 On paper, George Lucas' point about Grogu becoming a Jedi without going through the traditional milestones makes sense. On the other hand, the milestones in question have never been all that consistent. Even in the original trilogy, Luke (Mark Hamill) was rarely seen training in the grand scheme of things. A lightsaber 101 from Obi-Wan (Alec Guinness) on the Millennium Falcon, then some backflips on Dagobah with Yoda (Frank Oz), and Luke was apparently ready to take on Darth Vader (James Earl Jones, David Prowse).
 Meanwhile, Vader had decades of experience honing his craft with a lightsaber, and was gradually revealed via the prequels just how strong in the Force he was. In the Disney sequels, characters like Finn (John Boyega) and Rey (Daisy Ridley) similarly seemed naturally adept at Jedi-adjacent skills despite no formal training. Rey went on to have some training, but still not all that much.
 While Grogu was trained at the Jedi temple, he was still only young when Order 66 happened.
 So, the idea that Grogu has spent at least some time officially being trained by Luke seems like enough for Din Djarin's tiny green son to still be believably attuned to the Force. There doesn't need to be hours and hours of footage to support this, and some of Star Wars ' biggest characters in its most famous projects prove it.
